title: Configuration
description: The versioned artifact. A prompt alone is not a unit of version, comparison, or recommendation: its effectiveness inverts across model generations, and the same is true of pipeline depth and topology across throughput. Everything that can move the measured result belongs here, and configuration_id is the content hash of the rest.

configuration_id.description: sha256 over the canonical serialization of every other field. Also the cache key: a cache keyed on less than the full configuration returns confidently wrong results.

decoding.description: Recorded, never assumed. A harness that does not set temperature inherits the provider default — measured at 1.0 in a real safety codebase, producing up to 50% per-item verdict disagreement across identical runs.

temperature.description: null means the provider deprecated the parameter, which newer frontier models have done. null is a recorded fact, not an omission.

topology.description: Pipeline shape is a configuration dimension, not a fixed property of the system. A reflexive self-correcting architecture measured best at 1k documents/day and worst at 100k; the ranking inverts with load, so the shape must be selectable and measurable.

max_iterations.description: Required for reflexive topologies. The recorded hazard for verification loops is unbounded retry with no termination rule.

budget.description: What this configuration may spend, enforced BEFORE dispatch rather than observed after. Cost-driven degradation -- truncation, weaker-model fallback, aggressive caching -- degrades correctness without triggering any alert, which makes a budget a correctness constraint and not an economic one. on_exceed has no default because both behaviours are defensible and a silent choice between them is the failure mode.

gate_set_ref.description: Gates constrain a search; they are never a term in its objective. An optimizer that can move this is optimizing its own examiner.

router_policy_ref.description: The RoutingPolicy this configuration uses, or null for a single fixed model. This field existed from 1.0.0 with no description and was null everywhere -- declared, and meaning nothing. It is part of the hashed Configuration, so changing a routing policy produces a different configuration_id and the router is measured rather than deployed beside the measurement. A promotion justified by the COST a router saves, rather than by quality, is refused: an inconclusive quality comparison says the suite could not separate the two configurations, not that they are equivalent, and establishing equivalence needs a non-inferiority test against a declared margin.
